results.title: Scientists found the brain rhythm that makes your body feel like yours
results.content: # Scientists found the brain rhythm that makes your body feel like yours. :   A new study reveals that alpha brain waves help the brain decide what belongs to your body. A study from Karolinska Institutet, published in *Nature Communications*, explains how rhythmic brain activity known as alpha oscillations helps the brain separate the body from the outside world. The research provides new insight into how the brain combines information from different senses to maintain a stable feeling of bodily self. "Our findings help explain how the brain solves the challenge of integrating signals from the body to create a coherent sense of self," says Henrik Ehrsson, professor at the Department of Neuroscience, Karolinska Institutet, and senior author of the study. "Scientists found the brain rhythm that makes your body feel like yours." ScienceDaily. Scientists found the brain rhythm that makes your body feel like yours. In this talk I will present a set of scientific use cases where we have used scalable methods on high performance computing systems to optimize models in neuroscience research. The use cases include models from single cells, neural networks and whole brain models as well as spiking neural networks embedded in simulated agents.
